quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: What does an arrow painted on the pavement mean?

options.text: Drivers in that lane may make the movement shown by the arrow if they want to.
Drivers in that lane must make the movement shown by the arrow only if traffic lights are not working.
Drivers in that lane must always stop completely before making the movement shown by the arrow.
Drivers in that lane must make the movement shown by the arrow while following traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers in that lane must make the movement shown by the arrow while following traffic signals.
questions.explanation: An arrow painted on the pavement tells drivers in that lane to make the movement the arrow shows. Always follow traffic signs and signals before moving in the direction the arrow indicates.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the accident scene.
Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop at or near the accident scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if you can. Do not stand in traffic lanes because other vehicles could hit you. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and drivers can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction and drivers can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction and drivers cannot pass.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means drivers cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?

options.text: Whoever started moving last
The driver
Whoever is slower
The pedestrian

questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, whether or not there is a crosswalk.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Tow-away zone.
Steep downgrade.
Roadwork ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about road conditions and hazards ahead. This sign warns that the road may be slippery when wet.

questions.question: What do downward-facing triangular signs mean?

options.text: School zone ahead.
Yield to other traffic.
Construction zone ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.

questions.explanation: Downward-facing triangular signs tell drivers to yield. Wait until the road is clear and safe before you proceed.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: It is summer.
You must stop and back up immediately.
Driving conditions are not ideal.
You should drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange and warn that work is being done on or near the roadway. Drive carefully when you see these signs.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Winding road ahead.
No parking.
Right lane closed.
Multiple turns ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the road curves ahead and you should slow down.

questions.question: What are orange signs?

options.text: Work zone signs.
Regulatory signs.
School zone signs.
Guide signs.

questions.explanation: Orange signs are diamond-shaped with black letters or symbols. They warn that workers are on or near the highway.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Avoid stopping suddenly.
Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Release the gas pedal and let the car slow before braking.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to avoid hitting you. Release the gas pedal first to slow down, then press the brake pedal steadily. Your brake lights will turn on and your vehicle will stop smoothly.

questions.question: What is true about emergency vehicles?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and/or flashing lights.
They may use a loudspeaker to give instructions.
They may follow each other.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You must yield to police cars, fire engines, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using a siren or air horn and red or blue flashing lights. Follow any instructions from the emergency vehicle's loudspeaker. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only proceed when you are sure the road is clear.

questions.question: What affects how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: The amount of food in your stomach
Your body weight
How much time passes between drinks
All three choices

questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, the time between drinks, and your weight. Eating before or while drinking slows alcohol absorption, but it cannot prevent impairment if you drink too much.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs show?

options.text: Possible speeds for the area
The highest or lowest speed that is legally allowed
The speed to drive in heavy traffic
The speed to drive in poor conditions

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest speed that is legally allowed
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the highest or lowest safe speed allowed on a road. The maximum limits apply only in ideal conditions. You must drive slower when road conditions require it.

questions.question: When your car is in a line crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates:

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing the tracks.
Make sure your vehicle can cross all the way without stopping.
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can cross all the way without stopping.
questions.explanation: When following another vehicle at a railroad crossing, check that you have enough room to cross completely before entering the tracks. Never pass another vehicle at or near a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing any tracks.

questions.question: What do two solid yellow lines on the road mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is not allowed.
Passing is allowed if you are at the top of a hill.
Passing is allowed during the day only.

questions.explanation: Yellow lines mean traffic on the other side is moving in the opposite direction. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass from either direction.

questions.question: You are stopped in a line at a stop sign. The vehicles ahead have passed and there is no cross traffic. What should you do?

options.text: You may go through without stopping again.
You must stop again at the stop sign or line before going.
You may slowly roll past the stop sign.
You may follow the car ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop again at the stop sign or line before going.
questions.explanation: You must always come to a complete stop at a stop sign and yield to traffic before proceeding. Do not feel pressured by other traffic to skip the complete stop.

questions.question: Two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time. What happens?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers must use hand signals to communicate.
One driver should go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: Vehicles at a four-way stop go in order of arrival. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: How can you stay out of a truck or bus driver's blind spot?

options.text: Never pass them.
Do not drive alongside them and do not tailgate.
Flash your lights at them.
Sound your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive alongside them and do not tailgate.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles like trucks and buses have large blind spots on the sides and rear. Avoid driving beside them and never tailgate.

questions.question: What should you do on slippery roads?

options.text: Slow down.
Drive faster.
Drive at the speed limit with care.
Do not drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.explanation: Slow down when you see rain, snow, or ice, which make roads slippery. When road conditions are poor, you may need to drive slower than the speed limit for safety.

questions.question: What does a steady yellow light mean?

options.text: Go.
Yield to other cars.
Slow down and get ready to stop.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming soon. If you see yellow ahead, slow down and prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, proceed carefully through it.

questions.question: You notice a defect in your vehicle that may affect safe driving. What should you do?

options.text: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
Fix the defect when you have enough money.
Drive at slower speeds.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Any defect that may affect safe driving must be fixed right away. Do not drive the vehicle until it is fixed.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign do?

options.text: Warns of hazards that exist or may happen.
Alerts drivers to school zones.
Alerts drivers to public recreation areas.
Alerts drivers to food and gas locations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warns of hazards that exist or may happen.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of hazards that exist or may happen. These signs are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: When you park uphill on a street with a curb, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels to the left, away from the curb. If your brakes fail, your vehicle will roll into the curb instead of into traffic.

questions.question: What should you do when entering an interstate highway?

options.text: Stop on the entrance ramp and wait for an opening.
Drive on the shoulder until you can safely enter the main road.
Find a gap in traffic, adjust your speed, and merge safely.
Force your way into traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a gap in traffic, adjust your speed, and merge safely.
questions.explanation: Do not stop on the entrance ramp. Find a gap in traffic and adjust your speed to match it. Traffic on the interstate has the right-of-way.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic signal requires the same action as:

options.text: A slow sign.
A yield sign.
A stop sign.
An intersection sign.

questions.explanation: When you see a flashing red signal, you must stop and yield to all traffic that does not have to stop.
